title: Crash Course
description: A flat tire can ruin your day.  Now imagine that tire being on an F-15.  See how members from Kadena Air Base's 18th Equipment Maintenance Squadron partnered with Japan Air Self-Defense Force's 9th Air Wing to learn best practices on clearing a runway.

transcript.text: - So today we wrapped up the first
Joint United States Air Force
and Japan Air Self-Defense Force, or JASDF,
Crash Damaged and Disabled Aircraft Recovery training event.
Today we did debog,
which is the more common aircraft scenario you may run into.
Then we also went over how to use the disabled wheel dolly,
commonly referred to as the crash gate.
So if for some odd reason you can't use the aircraft wheel,
the tire blew, it's an assembly
that negates the need for the actual aircraft wheel.
The quicker we can get our air field cleared,
or the quicker the JASDF can get their air field cleared
and restore normal operations,
the less detriment that ripples across all of Japan
as far as diverted flights.
So the goal is to show them what we can do well
so that they can take those lessons back
and apply them at Naha
and so we can also see what they're doing well
so we can get better ourselves.
